notes:
Stage 0: merging origin/claude/rs-oppblind into the mainline conflicted only in RESULT.json (took mainline's; this file replaces it). decide.rs/mcts.rs/mod.rs/py_game.rs auto-merged with the Move struct / speed work; gate + goldens + audit-cross green with output unchanged before any stage-1 change (merge commit 24ec28e, pushed).
Default switch: Reveal::Fair is #[default]; the old behaviour is Reveal::Peek ('peek'). Every world draw (tree, worlds>1, rethink via worlds, window root fold, dialog/setup box commits) goes through sample_world, so the API, generation, arena and golden a1 all use fair unless told otherwise. PLAY_SIMS / PLAY_BUDGET / PLAY_WORLDS untouched. TreeMcts::run (not on the decide path) was switched to the fair sampler for consistency.
omniscient vs reveal: struct validation errors on omniscient + reveal != Fair (Fair = 'not specified'); the JSON layer additionally errors when the reveal key is given at all together with omniscient=true (even 'fair'), so an explicit fair+omniscient is not silently ignored.
Knowledge representation: per-card u8 bitmask CardInstance.known_by (bit 1<<seat), journaled (Undo::CardKnown) so search apply/rollback restores it. It is NOT serialized into the board JSON, hidden_json or card_record — that is what keeps the random-150 replay golden byte-identical. The spec said 'GameState の一部・記録と golden に載る'; I kept it in GameState but out of records/goldens because putting it in the board JSON would change every replay golden hash, contradicting the stronger invariant (random 150 unchanged). Consequence: a Game rebuilt from a record (from_hidden / replay) starts with empty knowledge (= nobody knows anything = maximally fair). The live API / generation / arena keep one Rust Game per match, so knowledge accumulates normally there. Measurement accessor: Game.knowledge_json(player_id).
Knowledge updates are done in the journal zone primitives (one place) instead of per effect: that covers every bounce/return-to-deck/field-to-life path without auditing each action. Effects only add LOOK (viewer), LOOK OPPONENT (viewer on opp deck top N), LOOK_LIFE (viewer = actor) and REVEAL (both, per target in flow::apply_target). shuffle_deck clears before the rng check (replay rngs do not shuffle, but the real game did).
Conservative choices ('迷ったら知らない側'): a card leaving hand/deck/face-down life keeps only its owner's bit — e.g. the opponent drawing a card I knew was on top of their deck (because it was returned there) becomes unknown to me, even though in reality I could follow it into their hand. Search-to-hand effects that do not emit a REVEAL action stay unknown to the opponent. 'Look at the opponent's hand' does not exist as an effect in the engine (would mark the viewer if added). Opponent temp_zone (transient) is still not shuffled, as in rs-reveal.
Owner bit on own hand cards and on cards the opponent alone knows can travel with a card when fair reshuffles it (the mask is per card, not per slot). Only bits of the drawing seat decide fixing, and all shuffled cards have that bit = 0, so fair itself is exact; in nested draws inside a world (opp_blind's opponent view) an opponent-only bit may sit at a reshuffled position — rare and only affects the measurement-only opp_blind.
Rules unchanged: golden-audit and random-150 replay are byte-identical after regeneration; tests_fair::knowledge_does_not_change_rules applies every legal move on a board with noisy masks vs zero masks and compares board (masks stripped), events and the next legal set. Two existing 'board unchanged' tests (LOOK OPPONENT, REVEAL) now compare with masks stripped and assert the new marks.
Encoder interaction (worth knowing for retraining): the scalar features read 'my remaining deck' aggregates (deck_aggregate / deck_apex over me.deck). Under peek that was the real deck, which leaked which of my cards sit in face-down life; under fair it is the world's deck (deck+life reshuffled), so root priors differ per world. tests/test_pimc_worlds.py asserted P identical across worlds; that check now runs under reveal='peek' and the default case only checks the wiring. Part of the -25..-35 price is this input shift (the net was trained on peek-era positions); retraining on fair-generated waves should absorb it.
a1 golden: all 50 games diverge; 30 of them at the very first decision (mulligan: the old search evaluated the redraw against the real deck order), median first divergence = step 1, mean 3.5, max 20; 174 of 5,639 old decisions are in the identical prefix; 19 winners changed. Decisions 5,639 -> 5,514.
Local arena: fair+knowledge vs peek = 36/80, wr 0.45, -34.9 Elo [0.346, 0.554], void 0 — matches the forecast (≈-25, price of fairness before retraining).
